tower-of-hanoi.title: Output move list as final answer
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After solving the puzzle, present the complete sequence of moves as a single list in the exact required format, placed as the final answer. Without this, the verifier cannot parse the moves.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the end of reasoning, when you have a full, legal move sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Providing no list or a partial list (e.g., missing closing brackets) leads to parsing failure.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Free blocked larger disks by moving top smaller disks first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If a larger disk is not the topmost disk on its peg, first move any smaller disks that sit above it to another peg where they can be placed legally. This clears the larger disk for the needed move.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever you need to move a disk that has smaller disks on top of it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 while disk 2 is on top of it, causing an illegal move.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate destination peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before moving a disk, check that the destination peg is empty or its top disk is larger than the moving disk. This prevents placing a larger disk onto a smaller one.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving disk 4 onto a peg where disk 2 is on top, which is illegal.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate source peg before each move
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Ensure that the disk you intend to move is the topmost disk on its source peg; moving any other disk violates the rules.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move disk 3 from a peg where disk 2 is on top.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Apply classic Hanoi recursion to generate move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When moving a stack of k disks from one peg to another using the third peg as auxiliary, recursively move k‑1 disks, then the largest, then the k‑1 disks again. This yields a correct sequence for sub‑towers.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When you need to relocate a contiguous sub‑tower of disks.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Failing to recursively move disks 1‑2 before moving disk 3, leading to an incomplete solution.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Clear destination peg of smaller disks before moving larger disk
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the destination peg currently holds smaller disks that must end up above the larger disk in the final configuration, move those smaller disks elsewhere before moving the larger disk onto the destination.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When a larger disk needs to be placed onto a peg that currently has smaller disks on top.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Trying to place disk 3 onto a peg where disk 1 is on top, blocking the correct final order.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Form classic start by moving smallest disk onto full stack
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the puzzle starts with all disks on one peg and the goal is to move them to another peg, begin by moving the smallest disk onto the target peg (which currently holds the full stack of larger disks), establishing the classic alternating pattern.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: In classic start‑to‑goal scenarios where the source peg holds the full ordered stack.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Starting with all disks on peg 0 and moving to peg 2, but moving a larger disk first, breaking the optimal pattern.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Goal‑first descending placement
tower-of-hanoi.principle: When the goal is to stack all disks on a single peg, always move the largest remaining disk that is not yet in place onto the goal peg before handling smaller ones. This ensures the final order is descending.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When constructing the final stack on a target peg.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Placing disk 2 onto the goal peg before disk 3, which later blocks placement of disk 3.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate final configuration after move generation
tower-of-hanoi.principle: After constructing the move list, simulate the moves from the initial state to verify that the final configuration matches the goal. This catches errors before submission.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: After you have generated the full move list, before outputting it.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Submitting a move list that leaves a disk on the wrong peg, causing verification failure.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Ensure non-empty move list when initial ≠ goal
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the initial configuration differs from the goal, generate at least one legal move; do not output an empty list. Verify that the move list changes the state toward the goal.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: At the start of solution generation, after checking that the puzzle is not already solved.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Returning [] (empty list) for a puzzle where disks need to be moved, leading to immediate rejection.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may assume no moves are needed or fail to generate any moves after reasoning.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Check whether the initial configuration matches the goal; if not, explicitly construct at least one legal move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Truncated move list (incomplete solution) due to token limit
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model runs out of generation budget before finishing the full sequence.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Plan the move sequence in concise steps or use recursion patterns that keep the list short.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a non‑top disk (source peg top mismatch)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model forgets to verify that the chosen disk is the topmost on its source peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always validate the source peg before each move.

tower-of-hanoi.description: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller disk (illegal placement)
tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model neglects to check the size relationship on the destination peg.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always validate the destination peg before each move.
